observations: Photo 0 shows a silver and black camera body with "Nikon" on the pentapult and "Z fc" on the top right; body cap is on the mount.
Photo 1 shows the top shutter-speed dial and a mounted lens with an aperture ring; "Nikon" and "Z fc" are visible on the body.
Photo 2 shows the complete kit: camera body, Nikon EN-EL25a battery, Nikon MH-32 charger, body cap, rear lens cap, and a front cap marked "TTArtisan APS-C 35mm F2.0".

claims.claim: Nikon Z fc retro-inspired SLR-style mirrorless camera
claims.evidence: photo 0, photo 1, photo 2 show the camera body and controls
sensor resolution cannot be confirmed from exterior photos

risks.risk: Camera does not power on, shutter fails, sensor or screen is defective
risks.proof: Video of camera turning on, navigating menus, and capturing a photo

risks.risk: Mounted lens is defective, focus/aperture rings are stuck, or the TTArtisan 35mm F2.0 is not the lens included
risks.proof: Clear photo of lens barrel text and video of focus and aperture rings turning

risks.risk: Battery or charger is dead or counterfeit
risks.proof: Video of battery charging in the MH-32 or powering the camera

risks.risk: Shutter count and wear are unknown
risks.proof: Screenshot of camera menu showing shutter count

proof_requests: Video of camera powering on, taking a photo, and reviewing the image
Clear photo of the lens barrel text and video of focus/aperture operation
Video of the battery charging in the Nikon MH-32 charger
Screenshot of the shutter count from the camera menu
response.reason: The Nikon Z fc is clearly identifiable from the photos, and the battery and charger are shown; since operation cannot be verified remotely, it is priced at its worst case as not working.
